after: The pipeline expansion supplies the Tennessee Valley Authority's new gas plant at the Kingston site in Tennessee. In February 2026 the authority said growing demand from data centers, population, and employment drove its decision to build the plant and keep the Kingston coal units running longer. The two sources are Enbridge's project page for the pipeline and a February 2026 news report on the authority's board vote.

A January 2026 trade report on the Intensity and Rainbow Energy Center announcement says the pipeline project, which includes the 208-mile Phase II extension from Washburn to Casselton, is meant to support sustained data center growth, grid reliability needs, and industrial development in North Dakota. The data center wording covers the project as a whole and no data center customer is named for Phase II.

Pipeline and Gas Journal reported in July 2025 that Northwest Pipeline's FERC application for the Wild Trail Project says the project was developed in response to strong demand to serve coal-to-gas power conversions, data centers, and industrial loads. No specific data center or plant is named.

The lateral delivers gas to the new Broadwing Energy plant in Decatur, Illinois, and to an Archer Daniels Midland facility, per a May 2025 federal notice. A Power Engineering report says Google will buy most of the Broadwing plant's power for its data centers, and ESG Today says the deal is meant to cover the energy needs of Google's growing data center footprint. No specific campus is named.

When Kinder Morgan launched the binding open season for this project in July 2024, its chief executive said the open season was part of meeting new gas demand for electric generation tied to artificial intelligence, cryptocurrency mining, data centers, and industrial reshoring. Data centers are one of several named drivers. No utility shipper or power plant fed by this expansion was found with its own data center tie.

The pipeline would carry gas to the planned 2,200 megawatt Dominion Energy and Santee Cooper gas plant on the former Canadys coal site in Colleton County, South Carolina. A May 2026 SC Daily Gazette report says utility executives call the plant essential for rapid population and industrial growth, and the reporter adds that this growth includes a ballooning number of energy-intensive data centers. The utilities' own approval statements found do not mention data centers. No single data center is named as a customer.

The expansion includes a 14.64 mile branch line and a new meter station for the Nebraska Public Power District Princeton Road power station, per a Federal Register notice from May 2026. The district's own page on its new generation says it expects unprecedented load growth and that much of the business interest it sees comes from agriculture-related operations and data centers. No single data center customer is named.

The pipeline connects the Mountain Valley Southgate project to Duke Energy Progress's new gas plant in Person County near Roxboro, and serves only that plant. A Canary Media report from February 2025 says the Person County plant is designed in part to meet rising demand expected from data centers and large new customers. No named data center customer was found.

The Wisconsin commission case page for the Paris engine plant places the seven gas engines, up to 128 megawatts, at the Lakeshore Capacity Improvement Project regulator station in the Town of Paris, which is the end of the Lakeshore Lateral. A Milwaukee public radio report on the May 2025 commission approval of the Paris and Oak Creek plants says We Energies points to a Microsoft data center being built in Racine County, and one commissioner cited data centers in southeastern Wisconsin as a reason for his vote.

The pipeline is the 19-mile service line that carries gas from the MountainWest Pipeline to the Aquila power plant in Eagle Mountain, Utah, being built by Williams. A February 2026 Eagle Mountain city hearing notice says Williams plans a natural gas power plant on the Stadion parcel to serve the Meta data center expansion. The notice does not use the name Aquila. The match rests on Williams, the Eagle Mountain location, and the Aquila project description in the Williams shipper meeting slides.

The Wisconsin commission case page for the Rochester Lateral says the pipeline will give firm gas to the proposed Oak Creek combustion turbine plant and the Paris engine plant, and later to the Elm Road station. A Milwaukee public radio report on the May 2025 commission approval of the Oak Creek and Paris plants says We Energies cited growing demand, including an incoming Microsoft data center in Racine County. A University of Wisconsin extension article gives the same link.
